record.paper_title: Recent Progress and Open Problems in Algorithmic Convex Geometry
record.original_question: Can the reflection walk based on a separation oracle be analyzed sharply enough to show that it needs only O*(nD) oracle calls for a convex body of diameter D, or even O*(n) oracle calls for isotropic bodies?

evidence.quote: It is possible that for this process, the number of oracle calls (not the number of Markov chain steps) is only O*(nD) rather than O*(n^2D^2), and even O*(n) for isotropic bodies. It is a very interesting open problem to analyze the reflection walk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a convex body of diameter $D$ accessed via a separation oracle: given a point $x \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the oracle either reports $x \in K$ or returns a halfspace $H \supseteq K$ that excludes $x$. Consider the following "reflection walk" used to sample (approximately) from the uniform distribution on $K$. From a current point $x \in K$, pick a uniformly random unit direction $u \in S^{n-1}$ and a step length (e.g.\ Gaussian or fixed); propose $y = x + tu$. If $y \in K$, move to $y$. Otherwise, query the separation oracle at $y$ to obtain a halfspace $H$ separating $y$ from $K$; reflect the trajectory across the boundary hyperplane of $H$ and continue, repeating reflections off oracle-supplied hyperplanes until either the reflected trajectory lies in $K$ (accept the resulting endpoint) or some termination rule is met (in which case stay at $x$).

Counting only oracle calls (not Markov-chain steps), prove or disprove the following bounds for mixing to within total-variation distance $\varepsilon$ of the uniform distribution on $K$, up to polylogarithmic factors in $n, D, 1/\varepsilon$ (denoted $O^*$):

(a) From any warm start, the reflection walk requires only $O^*(nD)$ separation-oracle calls for an arbitrary convex body $K$ of diameter $D$.

(b) When $K$ is in isotropic position (i.e.\ $K$ has unit covariance and barycenter at the origin, in which case $D = O^*(\sqrt{n})$ in expectation but here one asks the stronger statement), the reflection walk requires only $O^*(n)$ separation-oracle calls.

Establish a sharp analysis confirming these oracle-complexity bounds, or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.category_tag: Geometric random walks / sampling convex bodies
artifact.status_search_result: A search for sharp oracle-complexity analyses of the reflection walk on convex bodies given by a separation oracle did not surface a paper establishing the conjectured $O^*(nD)$ (general) or $O^*(n)$ (isotropic) bounds on the number of oracle calls. Subsequent work (e.g., Lee–Vempala on membership-oracle algorithms) has improved related sampling/optimization complexities, but a tight analysis of the reflection walk specifically achieving these bounds is not clearly documented.

status_evidence.title: Algorithmic Convex Geometry survey
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses random walks (ball walk, hit-and-run) and their mixing analyses for convex bodies given by oracles.
status_evidence.claim: No sharp analysis of the reflection walk achieving O*(nD) oracle calls is given.

status_evidence.title: Efficient Convex Optimization with Membership Oracles (Lee–Vempala)
status_evidence.snippet: Provides improved oracle complexity for convex optimization using random walks but does not specifically resolve the reflection walk oracle-call conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Related but does not establish the asked bounds for the reflection walk.
